The remote
HOME, holding HOME, holding OK and the app buttons

• HOME always brings you back to this home screen, from any app.
• Holding HOME opens the quick panel (Wi-Fi, timer, alarm, profiles, notifications).
• Holding OK on an app opens its menu: Move, Hide from the home screen or Uninstall.
• ▲ ▼ on an app stack switch which app is in front.
• Holding OK for 2 s on a poster or channel adds it to or removes it from your list.
• The Netflix and YouTube buttons on the remote open any app you want: press to open it, hold for 3 s to pick another app.
• The microphone button is still Google Assistant and Gemini.

In Settings › Home and automations › Automations, “When a button is pressed” gives a free button on the remote an app or a scene, with press, hold and double press.

If a button seems not to respond, Settings › Advanced › Extras › key tester shows every key the TV receives.
Home screen
Apps, stacks, hidden apps, themes, text size

The top bar shows Search, voice, the weather, the date and the time. Below are Live TV, Movies, Series, Network and your apps. The background and the details (rating, year and synopsis) follow what is selected.

Organizing apps:
• Hold OK on an app and choose Move. ◀ ▶ move it, OK confirms, ▲ hides it, ▼ goes back to the automatic order.
• Moving an app onto another one and pressing OK makes a stack.
• Hidden apps come back in Settings › Home screen › Hidden apps.
• Automatic stacks group loose apps by category; the stacks you made stay.

In Settings › Home screen:
• Theme: Dark (the art follows the selection) or Gallery (a different painting every day).
• Text size: Normal, Large or Larger, on every screen of the launcher.
• Quick panel tiles: which ones appear and in what order.
• More options: Simple mode (big cards and the name spoken aloud), read aloud what is selected, navigation sound, the “Now playing” pill, calendar of all accounts and “Today on TV” in Search.

With “Now playing” on, the top bar shows a pill with the cover and title of what is playing: OK pauses or resumes, holding OK opens the app.
Quick panel
Hold HOME: Wi-Fi, timer, alarm, profiles, notices

Hold HOME anywhere to open the quick panel.

Tiles:
• Wi-Fi and Bluetooth.
• Timer: each OK picks when the TV turns itself off; keep pressing to cancel.
• Sleep: turns the TV off now.
• Screensaver: starts the screensaver now.
• Audio: sound output (including a receiver over HDMI ARC).
• Alarm: opens the alarm clock.
• Guests: turns guest mode on or off.
• Home and Scenes: appear when there is Home Assistant or a scene.
• Night filter and DNS: hidden at first; show them in Settings › Home screen › Quick panel tiles.

The panel also has Profiles, what is playing (play, pause, next), notifications, the latest TV notices and the shopping list (OK crosses an item off). From there you can also open the launcher settings and the TV settings.
Voice and search
“Ok Google, open…” and the TV search

Search (at the top of the home screen) looks for channels, shows, movies, series and apps in one place. At the end of the results you can continue the same search on YouTube, Netflix or Prime Video.

Voice shortcuts. Say “Ok Google, open” and:
• Movies, Series, Network media, Home control, Search, Board or Scenes: opens that launcher screen.
• Remind me in 5 minutes (also 10, 15, 20 and 30): a timer with a notice. Cancel reminder cancels it.
• Hourglass: the stopwatch.
• Turn off in 30 minutes, Turn off in 1 hour or Keep the TV on.
• Weather report: reads the forecast aloud. Good morning: greeting, time, forecast and today's calendar.
• My calendar and TV diagnostics.

To ask for a channel in a sentence (“watch Globo”, “what's on SBT”), use “Ask the TV” in the phone panel, which accepts dictation from the keyboard microphone, or Claude. It works in English and Portuguese.
Weather, forecast and calendar
OK on the weather for the forecast, OK on the date for the calendar

The current weather comes from the nearest airport's report; the chance of rain is the median of three models.

• OK on the weather, at the top of the home screen, opens the forecast: the next 24 hours, a rain chart, 9 days, air quality, the sun and the moon.
• OK on the date opens the Google calendar of the TV's account. To combine all accounts, turn on “Calendar of all the TV's Google accounts together” in Settings › Home screen › More options.

In Settings › Home screen › Weather:
• Weather address: only needed if the TV can't find itself through Wi-Fi.
• Rain alert: a notice over the app when rain is about to start.
Screensaver and power
Screensaver, night filter, turning off by itself

The screensaver shows a greeting, the time, the date, the weather and cards in the corner (notifications, next alarm, messages). In the Gallery theme, the painting of the day moves slowly.

On the screensaver, ◀ ▶ move between the cards and OK dismisses the notice or pauses the music.

In Settings › Screen and power:
• Screensaver: how long the TV sits idle before it appears.
• Screensaver bottom row: Next hours or Day summary.
• Turn off when idle: warns 60 s before; any button cancels.
• Screensaver photos from your phone and Family board from your phone: a QR code opens the panel on the right page.
• More options: night filter (warmer screen at night), gentle shutdown (the timer dims the screen and lowers the volume in the last 5 minutes), family board on the screensaver, weekly recap, light mode and turn off when everyone leaves home (UniFi router).

The night filter hours are in Settings › Advanced › Extras. Photos from a network folder: open the folder in Network and choose “Use these photos in the screensaver”.
Alarm clock and timers
Alarms, timers with a notice, stopwatch, turning off

Alarm clock: hold HOME › Alarm › New alarm. ▲ ▼ change the hour and minute (hold to go fast) and OK picks the days. Each alarm can have a name, a sound (including an app or the last Live TV channel) and a volume.

At the time, the TV turns itself on over HDMI-CEC, the volume rises gradually and there is snooze. Stop opens Good morning. If the TV was off when an alarm was due, it tells you afterwards that it was missed.

Timers: up to 3 at once, with names (voice: “Ok Google, open Remind me in 10 minutes”). Hourglass is a stopwatch. The home screen shows the next one; on the stopwatch, OK stops it and shows the time.

Turning the TV off: the Timer tile in the quick panel or voice (“Turn off in 30 minutes”). “Keep the TV on” cancels.
Live TV
Channels from your IPTV list, guide, favorites, pause

Live TV uses YOUR IPTV account (Xtream Codes or an M3U list). The launcher comes with no channels. Add the account in Settings › TV and movies › Manage accounts.

Keys on a channel:
• ▲ ▼ change channel; ◀ goes back to the previous channel.
• OK opens the channel list; holding OK for 2 s makes it a favorite. The program Guide opens from the list.
• ▶▶ opens the channel options, such as pausing live TV.
• In the list, holding OK on a category hides it; ◀ shows the categories.

Pausing live TV: ⏯ (or ▶▶ › pause live) holds up to 2 minutes; OK resumes where you stopped and ▶ goes back to live.

Each account can have a 2nd XMLTV guide, which fills in the channels without a schedule. “My team” (from the phone panel) creates reminders for your team's games.
Movies, series and Network
Catalog, continue watching, subtitles, home servers

Movies and Series come from the same IPTV account (also from an M3U list), with poster, rating, synopsis and “continue where you stopped”.

• Movies: Filter (genre, era, minimum rating, unwatched only), Pick a random movie and “This movie's collection” on the details page.
• In the player, ▼ opens the menu: audio, subtitles and subtitle size, “Turn off the TV when this ends” and marking the intro (afterwards you get “Skip intro · OK”).
• Series: the next episode starts after a 10 s countdown; after 3 in a row, the TV asks whether you are still watching.
• Preferred audio (original with subtitles or dubbed) and online subtitles (OpenSubtitles): Settings › TV and movies.

Network: videos, music and photos from Plex, Jellyfin, Emby, PC or NAS folders (SMB, WebDAV) and UPnP. Servers that are on show up by themselves; others go in Add, on the same screen.
Profiles, kids and guests
Profiles, kid profile, PIN, bedtime, guests

Profiles: hold HOME › Profiles. Each Google account on the TV has its own channel favorites, continue watching, last episodes and app order. “Add profile” signs in with another account.

Kid profile: in the quick panel, mark a profile as a kid profile (asks for the parents' PIN, which is the web panel PIN). On it, kids mode and bedtime turn on by themselves, and leaving asks for the PIN.

In Settings › Family:
• Parental controls: blocked channels and categories disappear everywhere and don't play. To watch: in the player, OK › Filters › “Show hidden categories and blocked channels” and the PIN.
• Kids mode: only categories marked as kids' show in Live TV, Movies and Series.
• Kids PIN: a second PIN that unlocks channels and bedtime without giving away the panel PIN.
• More options: Bedtime (during the hours, only allowed apps open and the volume has a ceiling), Daily screen time and Ask for the PIN to change the HOME.
• Guests: guest mode hides the profile, the calendar and the apps you pick. Guest Wi-Fi: type it once and guests scan a QR code.
Home and automations
Home Assistant, scenes, routines and buttons

Home (Home Assistant): lights, plugs, fans, covers, scenes, sensors and air conditioning. Open it from the Home tile in the quick panel or with “Ok Google, open Home control”.
• OK turns things on or off. Holding OK on a light sets the brightness; on a color light, ▲ ▼ change the tone. On the air conditioner, holding OK changes the temperature.
• OK on a camera shows the current snapshot. When the doorbell rings, the snapshot pops up over what you are watching.
• Home Assistant address and token: Settings › Home and automations › Home Assistant from your phone.

Automations (Settings › Home and automations › Automations) collect everything the TV does by itself:
• When it is time: turn on, open an app, run a scene or turn off, on the days you choose.
• When a button is pressed: press, hold or double press opens an app or runs a scene.
• When something happens: a movie started, a movie paused or ended, the TV turned on, everyone left, rain is coming.
• By link: each scene has a link.

Scenes are created and tested in the web panel › Extras › Scenes. Run one from the Scenes tile in the quick panel.
LG TV volume
LG NetCast (2013): real volume over the network
Web panel on your phone
Control the TV from a phone or computer at home

The web panel opens in the browser of any phone or computer on the same network.

Turning it on: Settings › Remote access. Set a PIN (the same one is used for parental controls and for Claude) and open the address shown there in a browser. “Sign in from your phone” shows a QR code: the phone scans it and signs in without typing the PIN.

In the panel:
• Ask the TV: type or dictate “watch Globo”, “open YouTube”, “remind me in 7 minutes”, “turn off in 30 minutes”.
• Remote control, the TV screen live and typing with accents.
• Install and remove apps (including .apks and .xapk), the curated store and files.
• Screensaver photos, family board, scenes, Home Assistant, My team, router and backups.
• TV diary: 7 days of what touched the TV.

Installed as an app on the phone, the panel shows up in Share: a YouTube video opens in the TV's YouTube, a link opens on the TV and text becomes a message.

The panel is in English when the browser is not in Portuguese. Actions that delete something ask for the PIN again.
Claude and other AIs
Ask in plain language; you choose what the AI may do

The launcher has an MCP server: Claude, ChatGPT and other AI apps control the TV over the internet, through a Tailscale tunnel that runs inside the app.

Turning it on: Settings › Remote access › Claude over the internet (MCP) › Connect (QR code). The walkthrough shows the Tailscale sign-in and the address to paste into the AI app. Sign-in uses the panel PIN or a Google account on the TV.

Examples: “what's on the TV?”, “alarm at 6:30 on weekdays”, “add milk to the shopping list”, “why is the internet slow?”.

You choose how much power it has in Settings › Advanced › Confirmations: ask on the TV, allow or block each kind of action. “Shell for Claude” and “Let Claude see the screen” are separate switches; the TV shows a notice every time the screen is seen. “Claude sign-ins” revokes all access.
Backup and restore
A password-locked backup, every night

Settings › System › Automatic backup.

• Set the backup password (8 characters or more) and write it down somewhere safe: without it, nobody can open the copy, not even you.
• Every night, while the TV is idle, it saves a full backup locked with that password. The last 7 are kept, and every night it checks that the copy would restore.
• Back up now: a backup right away.
• Extra copy: connect a Google Drive account and the copies also go to the OneTV-backup folder, visible in your Drive.
• Restore from Google Drive: pick the copy and type the password; the launcher restarts by itself.

You can also download and restore a backup from the web panel.
Updates and problems
New versions, what changed, diagnostics

Settings › System:
• Diagnose the TV: internet, DNS, VPN and why an app stopped, all at once (or “Ok Google, open TV diagnostics”).
• Check for a new version: the launcher checks by itself and installs with the screen off; here you check right away.
• What changed: what is new in the installed version.
• Check on the TV: a short checklist to try what changed with the remote.
• What gets used: screens and options by use, counted only on this TV.
• Safe mode: appears only if a new version crashed right after installing.

Android system updates wait for the early morning (3 to 5 am), so they don't interrupt a movie.

Settings › Advanced has the network (Private DNS, speed test), Extras, hidden factory apps, permissions and the launcher's own shell. You rarely need to touch it.
